task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=3 and h a smooth positive Hermitian form. Fix a smooth strictly positive probability dV, use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and use genuine canonical h-plurisubharmonic representatives. Define v_minus(h)=inf{integral_X(h+dd^c u)^n:u is bounded and h-psh}; assume v_minus(h)=0. This is the bounded-potential mass infimum, not the fixed-density Gauduchon volume.
For nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), b_h(f)>=0 is the maximal coefficient of a genuine subsolution MA_h^ext(u)>=b_h(f)f dV, equivalently the limit of continuous-equation normalization scalars of min(f,k). The extended non-pluripolar measure is defined by finite-level truncation and can have infinite total mass.
For a measurable real or complex root p in Ln(dV), set rho_h(p)=b_h(|p|^n)^(-1/n), taking rho_h(0)=0 and infinite value for a zero threshold. Equivalently rho_h(p)=sup_T integral_X |p| k_T dV, with T smooth positive (n-1,n-1), dd^c T=0, integral_X h wedge T=1, T=gamma^(n-1), and k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n). The supremum uses all such tests. Set D_h={p in Ln:rho_h(p)<infinity} with norm ||p||_Ln+rho_h(p), and D_h^0 the closure of bounded measurable roots in that norm.
Original S04 has two questions. First, must D_h^0=D_h when v_minus(h)=0? Equivalently must every finite positive-threshold root p satisfy rho_h(|p| 1_{|p|>K})->0 as K tends to infinity, or can a positive-threshold root have nonvanishing uniform tails? Second, do these uniform root tails suffice for the exact finite-mass equation in P07: for nonzero f>=0 in L1 with b_h(f)>0 and f^(1/n) in D_h^0, does some genuine h-psh u satisfy MA_h^ext(u)=b_h(f) f dV, in a rigorously specified natural singularity or envelope class?
Known background: p in D_h^0 iff the displayed root-tail norm tends to zero, equivalently norm convergence under every dominated perturbation tending to zero in smooth-volume measure. Smooth roots are dense in D_h^0, which contains Lr for r>n. At positive lower mass both spaces equal Ln, so that regime does not resolve this question. Uniform root tails give scalar continuity, dual attainment and error moduli for exponential approximations. They do not in the known argument supply capacity compactness or a smaller-background envelope for potentials. Every positive threshold is attained by a subsolution, possibly with excess or infinite mass; Lp densities for p>1 have a continuous exact solution. The general L1 exact equation at zero lower mass remains open. An abstract Banach-function-space example or failure of an endpoint bound does not exhibit a root on an actual compact Hermitian manifold. No candidate root, geometry, conclusion or proof is supplied.

# Restricted S04 power-capacity reconstruction targets

Use a connected compact complex X of dimension n>=3, a smooth positive
Hermitian h, a fixed smooth positive probability dV, and
D=i partial barpartial/(2pi). Use actual canonical genuine potentials and
ordinary wedges. No closedness, BMP or positive lower mass is assumed.
Keep all original S04 background: b_h(g) is the maximal subsolution
coefficient and decreasing scalar limit for min(g,j); rho_h(p) is
b_h(|p|^n)^(-1/n), equivalently the supremum over ALL original smooth
positive D-closed Gauduchon tests normalized by int h wedge T=1.
D_h^0 is the closure of bounded measurable roots in ||p||Ln+rho_h(p),
equivalently the vanishing original root-tail condition.
Let cap_h(E)=sup_(0<=w<=1, genuine h-psh) MA_h(w)(E).

A. Suppose 0!=f>=0 in L1(dV) and there are A,alpha>0 such that
int_E f dV <= A cap_h(E)^(1+alpha) for EVERY Borel E.
For EVERY nonzero measurable 0<=g<=f,
b_h(g)>=C (int g dV)^(-alpha/(1+alpha)), and
rho_h(g^(1/n))<=C^(-1/n)(int g dV)^(alpha/(n(1+alpha)))
with one C>0 depending only on X,h,A,alpha. Preserve the ENTIRE
original test supremum, not a selected invariant family. In particular
f^(1/n) lies in D_h^0, with this quantitative tail estimate.

B. Under A there exists a bounded continuous genuine h-psh phi with
sup_X phi=0 and the EXACT actual equation MA_h(phi)=b_h(f) f dV.
The coefficient and actual total mass are finite and strictly positive.
Specify and prove potential compactness and actual Hermitian product
passage; scalar convergence alone does not imply the equation. No uniform
higher Lp norm of the clips may be assumed. No homogeneous uniqueness claim.

C. For any fixed positive smooth Hermitian theta, if continuous genuine
theta-psh u_j lie in [-1,0], their measures all obey one common bound
A_0 cap_theta^(1+alpha), and
int |u_j-u_k| MA_theta(u_j)->0 as BOTH indices tend to infinity,
then u_j is uniformly Cauchy. Reconstruct this stability assertion with
all torsion effects and legal competitor bounds retained.

D. For EVERY given X,h,dV and alpha>0 choose a small holomorphic ball
R=|z|<1 about p, a smooth cutoff chi equal to1 on a smaller ball and
supported in the former, q(s)=(1-s)^(-alpha), q(-infinity)=0,
psi=chi q(log R^2)+1-chi, extended1 outside. For some sufficiently
small delta>0, u=delta psi-sup_X(delta psi) is bounded continuous genuine
h-psh with h+Du>=h/2 and actual MA_h(u)=f dV. This f is in L1, has
f>=c>0 almost everywhere, and belongs to NO Lp for p>1.
It satisfies the power-capacity hypothesis in A for every Borel set,
has b_h(f)=1, and
rho_h(f^(1/n) 1_(f>K))<=C(log K)^(-alpha) for large K.
Check the exact pure inner top density against Euclidean volume:
delta^n n! alpha^n(alpha+1)/pi^n * R^(-2n)
 * (1-log R^2)^(-n(alpha+1)-1),
and exact ball mass delta^n alpha^n(1-log r^2)^(-n(alpha+1)).
Prove absence of an origin atom and global absolute continuity for actual
bounded Hermitian products, including all lower mixed terms and the cutoff.
This applies to any GIVEN h with v_minus(h)=0 as well; it does not assert
that arbitrary h has zero lower mass. The reference is not Holder at p.

E. Judge the exact original completion criterion separately. The extra
power-capacity assumption is not known to follow from arbitrary positive
threshold or uniform root tails. A--D prove neither D_h=D_h^0 for all
positive-threshold roots nor the exact equation for ALL D_h^0 roots.
The explicit datum is not a bad-tail counterexample. Historical capacity
and bounded-range results must be attributed; no literature priority is
certified. Retain the entire original problem and completion criteria.

Independently reconstruct or reject every stated target. Find and check
each indispensable primary premise, its full hypotheses, and numeric
operator conventions. No author paper, proof, verdict or trusted notes

task.completionCriteria:
Resolve either original question in full by a complete proof or an actual compact Hermitian counterexample. For the first negative answer give explicit X,h,dV,p with v_minus(h)=0, p in Ln, finite rho_h(p) and a strictly positive lower limit for its tail norms, proving all of these from the full test formula or genuine subsolutions. For a positive answer prove every such root is order-continuous without imposing positive lower mass or stronger density integrability. For the second question retain the exact threshold and finite prescribed measure, specify the equation class, and prove the required compactness/product passage; scalar and measure convergence alone do not suffice. Distinguish the two questions if only one is answered, and do not infer whole-family potential uniqueness. Verify pivotal external statements at primary sources and independently reconstruct the complete result.
Independently reconstruct or reject A--E under the explicitly additional capacity hypothesis. Judge full original completion separately; preserving a restricted result does not answer either unrestricted universal question.
